precepts.text: When Israel went out of Egypt, Judah was his sanctuary and Israel his dominion; the sea saw it and fled, Jordan was driven back, because the Lord was dwelling within his people.
precepts.point: When the Lord is dwelling within Israel, the creation itself moves for them; only for the Israelites will a river fall back. You do not know the manner of love the Most High bestowed upon this people to call them the children of God.
precepts.why:
“When Israel went out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a people of strange language; Judah was his sanctuary, and Israel his dominion. The sea saw it, and fled: Jordan was driven back.” Judah was his sanctuary and Israel his dominion: the Lord was dwelling within his people, and because of that the sea fled and Jordan was driven back.

That is what happened when the feet of the priests bearing the ark were dipped in the brim of the water. Jordan overflows all his banks all the time of harvest, yet the waters from above rose up upon an heap very far from the city Adam and those coming down toward the salt sea failed and were cut off, and the priests stood firm on dry ground in the midst of Jordan. No man can stand in a river, but when the Lord is dwelling within Israel, the creation itself moves for them; only for the Israelites will a river fall back.

You do not know the manner of love the Most High bestowed upon this people to call them the children of God.

This is a very brief and quick reading, but overall we see it talking about those that are blessed, those being blessed that keep the commandments. It says who is like the Most High, and then it gives praise to God who delivered Israel. It is still good to read; it is a good refresher, especially Psalms 111 and 112, and there is always a takeaway from the readings that we do.
